subtitle: Workout log, on your wrist
promotional_text: Now on Apple Watch: log sets from your wrist with Siri, rest timers and Apple Health. Templates, plate calculator and iCloud sync on iPhone.
description:
Flex is the ultimate companion for your strength training journey. Whether you're a powerlifter, bodybuilder, or just getting started in the gym, Flex helps you track your progress, build strength, and achieve your fitness goals with simplicity and precision.

Experience effortless workout tracking designed to keep you focused on your lift, not your phone. You can build personalized workout templates for any routine and organize them into custom folders to keep your training schedule clean and accessible. With the built-in Smart Plate Calculator, you never have to do gym math again.... Flex automatically visualizes how to load the bar for your specific lifts.

Flex is on your wrist too. Start any template from Apple Watch, set the weight and reps with the Digital Crown, rest on a wrist-tap timer and finish with your iPhone in the locker; the workout lands in History the moment the two meet. With your phone along, both show the same workout live. Say "Log bench press in Flex" to Siri to log a set hands-free, let Apple Health record your heart rate and calories, and keep this week's count on your watch face.

Your workouts go where you go. Flex seamlessly syncs your data across all your devices using iCloud, so your history is always up to date. Designed with privacy in mind, Flex uses Sign in with Apple and iCloud to ensure your health data remains secure without third-party accounts. Build consistency and see results. Download Flex today and make every rep count.

Flex is designed and built by two fitness freaks, Ashton Krstolic and Kevin Brown. Every feature exists because we needed it at the rack. Questions or ideas? Visit our support page — we read every message.
whats_new:
• Flex on Apple Watch: start any template from your wrist, log sets with the Digital Crown, rest on a wrist-tap timer and finish, with your iPhone in the locker. Finished workouts land in History when the two meet.
• Phone and watch show the same workout live: tick a set on one and it is ticked on the other; finish on either.
• A rest timer on both devices, with its default in Settings.
• Siri: "Log bench press in Flex" logs a set on iPhone or Apple Watch.
• Apple Health: watch workouts record heart rate and calories and count toward your rings.
• A watch-face complication shows this week's workouts against your goal.
• A workout in progress now survives Flex being closed.

review_info.purpose: Flex is a strength-training log for iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch. People build workout templates, log each set's weight and reps (with a plate calculator for barbell lifts and a rest timer), and see their history, personal records and weekly goals. It replaces a paper or spreadsheet gym log, and the watch app lets them log sets with the phone in a locker.
review_info.audience: People who lift weights, from beginners to powerlifters and bodybuilders. There is no age-specific content.
review_info.setup:
No demo account is needed: Sign in with Apple accepts any Apple Account.
- Launch Flex and tap Sign in with Apple on the welcome screen.
- Workout tab › Start Empty Workout › Add Exercises, or tap a template and Start Workout. Tap a weight or reps cell for the keypad; barbell exercises show a plate calculator. Tick a set to start the rest timer, then Finish.
- History, Profile (goals and charts) and Exercises show the saved data.
- Apple Watch (optional): the watch app installs with Flex. Start a template on the watch, set weight and reps with the Digital Crown, and Finish; the workout appears in History on the iPhone. The iPhone app can be reviewed in full without a watch.
external_services: iCloud (CloudKit): syncs the person's workouts, templates and exercises through their own private iCloud database; Flex has no servers
iCloud key-value storage: syncs preferences and the Sign in with Apple identifier, name and email between the person's devices
Sign in with Apple: the only sign-in

HealthKit (Apple Health): with permission, a workout done on Apple Watch is saved to Apple Health with heart rate and active calories, and the iPhone shows that workout's live heart rate. Flex never copies Health data into its own storage
review_info.services_note: Flex has no servers of its own and no third-party SDKs: no analytics, advertising, payment or AI services. Apple Watch and iPhone talk over Watch Connectivity.
review_info.regions: None. Flex works the same in every region. Version 1.1.0 is in English only.
review_info.regulated: Not applicable. Flex is a workout log, not a medical device, and gives no medical advice; heart rate is shown from Apple Health only during a watch workout. The exercise library, icon and text are our own.

demo_account.not_needed: Sign in with Apple is the only sign-in and accepts any Apple Account; Flex has no passwords of its own.

review_info.account_deletion: Profile tab › Settings (gear, top right) › Account › Delete Account, then Delete Account in the confirmation. It erases every workout, template, custom exercise and preference from the device and the person's iCloud and signs them out, returning to the welcome screen.
review_info.health_ui: Profile tab › Settings (gear, top right) › Apple Health, which says what Flex saves to and reads from Health; during a workout started on Apple Watch, the iPhone's live heart rate reads "♥ 128 · Apple Health".

review_recording.shows: It starts on the Home Screen, launches Flex signed out, signs in with Sign in with Apple, opens Profile › Settings to show the Apple Health section (what Flex saves to and reads from Health), then goes to Account › Delete Account, confirms, and ends back on the welcome screen with the account deleted.

review_notes:
In reply to the review of 12 November 2026 (submission 43622ff7-651f-497c-b126-ce423c9e1469), build 11:
- 5.1.1(v): Settings › Account › Delete Account now erases everything Flex holds and signs the person out. Flex has no server, so there is no Apple token to revoke; a person can also stop using Sign in with Apple for Flex in iOS Settings › Apple Account › Sign-In & Security › Sign in with Apple.
- 2.5.1: Settings has an Apple Health section that says what Flex saves to and reads from Health, and the live heart rate during a watch workout reads "♥ 128 · Apple Health".

min_ios.reason: The tab bar is built on the iOS 18 Tab API, and iOS 17 runs on exactly the same iPhones (XS, XR and later), so a lower floor would add no devices; SwiftData closes iOS 16. Decided by the owner 2026-11-10 (STORY_012).

english_only.reason: 1.1.0 is the Apple Watch release, built before the ten-language rule existed (2026-11-10) and with no string catalog yet; the owner chose to ship the watch first. BACKLOG_001 carries the ten languages (the whole UI and the 226 exercise names) to 1.2.0.
